images.caption: Figure 1:Frontier3DBench: 145 tasks in 9 categories spanning objects (L1), scenes (L2), and interactive open worlds (L3). Right: leaderboard of the 11 model–harness configurations (0–100,↑\uparrow).

Figure 2:Task formulation. Agents receive instructions and optional references or initial assets, then produce code and assets for Blender objects and scenes (L1/L2) or Unreal Engine open worlds (L3).

Table 3:Performance on 145 tasks (0–100,↑\uparrow), ranked by Total, the overall score (Eq.2). T2C: Text2Code; I2C: Img2Code; SV: SingleView; B2S: Brief2Scene; R2S: Ref2Scene; RP: RealPhoto; SE: SceneEdit; T2E: Text2Env; I2E: Img2Env.

Figure 5:Overall score versus estimated average API cost per task across 145 tasks (log scale). Markers and the Pareto frontier use cost-range midpoints. Vertical bars show 95% task-bootstrap intervals for the overall score.
Figure 6:Object, scene, and interactive-world examples. Parentheses show task scores (0–100). World views are rendered from model-specific cameras. Minecraft reference: Akirby80.

Figure 7:Additional visual comparisons across objects, scenes, and interactive worlds.Columns group cases; rows show references and model outputs.(a)Four object and three scene cases compare runs of GPT-6.1-sol, DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash, Kimi-K3.1-Pro, and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.(b)Three world cases each show two submitted project previews from GPT-6-astra, GPT-6.1-sol, and GPT-6-luna.
Cases are drawn from the 145-task suite.
World views use model-specific cameras; Valentine uses the same reference for both views.
